subtopics.title: The Data Cycle and the Question Worth Asking

questions.question: Which of these is the correct order of the data cycle?
options: Collect, pose a question, summarise, organise, report
Pose a question, collect, organise and classify, summarise and represent, analyse, report
Summarise, collect, pose a question, report, organise
Organise, collect, analyse, pose a question, report

questions.question: A patient's waiting time of 47,5 minutes is an example of which type of data?
options: Categorical data
Discrete numerical data
Continuous numerical data
Secondary categorical data

questions.question: The class uses the clinic's own register instead of standing at the door with a clipboard. This makes the data:
options: secondary data, because they were recorded by someone else for another purpose
primary data, because the class is using them for its own question
categorical data, because a register contains names
biased data, because registers are never accurate

questions.question: Which choice would have introduced the most serious bias into the clinic study?
options: Recording times to the nearest minute
Recording only the patients who arrived at eight o'clock, or only those who complained
Recording fifteen patients spread across the morning
Using the register rather than asking patients to estimate

subtopics.title: Tallies, Frequency Tables and Class Intervals

questions.question: In the class's frequency table, the interval 30 to 59 minutes has a frequency of:
Why are intervals of "0 to 30" and "30 to 60" unacceptable?
options: Because the intervals are too wide
Because they overlap, so a wait of exactly 30 minutes belongs in two rows
Because intervals must always start at 1
Because continuous data may not be grouped at all

questions.question: What check should be done on every frequency table before it is used?
options: That the frequencies add up to the number of values collected
That every interval has at least one value in it
That the largest frequency appears in the first row
That the intervals are listed from largest to smallest

questions.question: What is lost when continuous data are grouped into class intervals?
options: Nothing — the table contains all the original information
The total number of values
The individual values themselves, so exact figures such as three waits of 45 minutes can no longer be read off
The unit of measurement

questions.question: The fifteen waiting times total 825 minutes. What is the mean?
options: 45 minutes
55 minutes
60 minutes
82,5 minutes

questions.question: For the fifteen ordered values, which position holds the median, and what is it?
options: Position 7,5; median 42,5 minutes
Position 8; median 45 minutes
Position 8; median 55 minutes
Position 15; median 140 minutes

questions.question: The range of the waiting times is:
options: 120 minutes
45 minutes
55 minutes
140 minutes

questions.question: Which measure of centre can be used for categorical data such as the reason for a clinic visit?
options: The mean
The median
The range
The mode

questions.question: Why is the mean of 55 minutes higher than the median of 45 minutes?
options: Because the mode is also 45
Because three patients waited 90, 120 and 140 minutes, and those outliers pull the mean upward
Because the median was calculated from unordered data
Because 15 is an odd number of values

questions.question: The provincial office wants to know the total nursing time consumed by the morning. Which summary rebuilds that total?
options: The mean, because mean × number of patients gives back 825 minutes
The median, because it is the typical wait
The mode, because it is the most common wait
The range, because it covers all the values

questions.question: What is the stated weakness of the range?
options: It cannot be calculated for continuous data
It always equals the mean minus the median
It is computed from only two values, so a single unusual case can distort it
It ignores the largest value in the data set

questions.question: Which conclusion best matches the clinic's data?
options: Every patient waits about an hour, so the queue should be shortened across the board
The typical wait is 45 minutes; the real problem is a long tail of very long waits
The clinic is fast, since the mode is only 45 minutes
Nothing can be concluded, because the mean and median disagree

subtopics.title: Asking a Question the Numbers Can Answer

questions.question: Why is "Do we spend too much on airtime?" a poor question to investigate?
options: Because airtime spending is categorical data
Because "too much" cannot be measured, so no number could settle it
Because it asks about a household rather than a school
Because it needs a tally table

questions.question: Which of these can NOT be added together?
options: Rands spent on data by each person
Minutes waited by each patient
Learners counted in each class
The networks people use, such as Telkom and Vodacom

questions.question: "Don't you agree the queue is terrible?" is a poor survey question because it:
options: leans towards the answer it wants, instead of asking neutrally
produces continuous data instead of discrete data
cannot be tallied
requires secondary data

questions.question: What is the first thing to do with a jumbled list of values?
options: Calculate the average
Put them in order from smallest to largest
Draw a graph
Round them all to the nearest ten

questions.question: In a tally, why is every fifth stroke drawn across the four before it?
options: To show that value is the mode
To mark the end of a class interval
So the marks count themselves in fives and are easy to total
To indicate an outlier

questions.question: The five piles of clinic waits contain 3, 8, 1, 1 and 2 patients. What does adding them confirm?
options: That the mode is in the second pile
That the intervals do not overlap
That the range is 120 minutes
That all 15 patients have been counted once, with none lost or double-counted

subtopics.title: The Middle, the Most, the Average and the Stretch

questions.question: The Simplifier calls the mean the "sharing-out number". For the clinic data that number is:
options: 55 minutes
45 minutes
825 minutes
120 minutes

questions.question: If there had been an EVEN number of patients, how would the middle value be found?
options: Take the larger of the two middle values
Take the two middle values and split the difference between them
Use the mode instead
The median cannot be found for an even number of values

questions.question: Which everyday comparison does the Simplifier use for the mean being dragged upward?
options: A taxi that is always full
One uncle with a big salary lifting the "average income" of a struggling family
A tally that has been counted twice
A washing basket that never empties

questions.question: What does the Simplifier say a complete answer must include, beyond the number itself?
options: A second calculation using a different method
A graph of the data
The unit, and a plain sentence about what should actually be done
The raw data listed in full
